readout_other: Multielectrode array extracellular recording of retinal ganglion cell spiking
direction_notes: US directly evoked precisely timed ganglion-cell spiking (excitatory), while simultaneously modulating visual sensitivity in a spatially dependent way: sensitivity decreased near the US focus and increased at a distance, and increased locally at US offset.

exposures.label: Focused ultrasound stimulation of the isolated salamander retina at 43 MHz

timing.protocol_description: For most experiments, this consisted of 1 s of stimulus On and 1 s of stimulus Off, repeated for many cycles, for a total duration of 1-5 min. In some experiments, the On and Off times were varied randomly to make a binary noise stimulus sampled at 30 Hz to match the temporal structure of visual stimuli. High-frequency sub-modulation of the 43 MHz carrier within each On pulse (10 Hz to 1 MHz) was tested and found to have no effect on responses when average power was held constant, so it was eliminated in favor of a continuous carrier for the On period.

source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: The US transducer was a custom-made, focused delay line transducer with a Lithium Niobate active element and a fused quartz focusing lens, and was operated at the designed center acoustic frequency of 43 MHz.
source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.ispta_w_: A stimulus frequency of 0.5 Hz was used, and average power was varied between 0.03 and 30 $\mathrm { W } / { \mathrm { c m } } ^ { 2 }$ (Fig. 3a).
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_duration_ms: For most experiments, this consisted of 1 s of stimulus On and 1 s of stimulus Off, repeated for many cycles, for a total duration of 1–5 min.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_repetition_fre: The 43 MHz carrier was modulated at low frequencies (0.5–15 Hz) to match the temporal pattern used for visual stimulation (Fig. 1c).
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.duty_cycle_pct: The calculated time-averaged acoustic power was $1 0 { - } 3 0 \ \mathrm { W / c m } ^ { 2 }$ for 50% duty cycle stimulus (e.g., 1 s On, 1 s Off) for most experiments (exceptions noted).
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: For most experiments, this consisted of 1 s of stimulus On and 1 s of stimulus Off, repeated for many cycles, for a total duration of 1–5 min.

flags.reason: The paper states 'time-averaged acoustic power' calculated from an insertion-loss calibration curve (measured in a water bath, not explicitly labelled free-field or in-situ), so the value is placed in unspecified_domain; recorded under ispta_w_cm2 though spatial averaging (peak vs average) is not specified.

180 W/cm2 was the maximum power used in a separate CdCl2 synaptic-block experiment ('The stimulus was repeated at progressively higher-power levels up to 180 W/cm2'), included in the list alongside the main 0.03-30 W/cm2 sweep.
The paper reports numbers of cells analysed per figure/comparison but never states the total number of retinas or salamanders used.

Effects were mixed: direct excitatory spiking responses to US onset/offset, plus bidirectional (increase or decrease) modulation of visual sensitivity depending on distance from the US focus and On vs Off timing.
